TheobjectinspectionCONOPrequiresstatistically-supported methods to determine emitted spectrum and/or configuration of mass within a container, and the R&D needed to achieve those goals would likewise apply to several other applications. 4.5 Nuclear Treaty Verification A potential use of SDF is in Arm Control Treaty (ACT) verification. ACT verification has two major thrusts. One is to ensure that the operations occurring at nuclear facilities that have been subjected to a treaty agreement can be monitored and confirmed, termed nuclear compliance verification (NCV) and the other is to verify that the parties to a treaty have no more than an agreed upon number of nuclear weapons in each of various states of readiness and to verify agreed-upon dismantlement activities. 4.5.1 Warhead Verification Ultimately (and simplistically), weapons and warhead verification is a counting exercise. The locations of the NW (nuclear weapons) are assumed known to the parties of the treaty. An important aspect of ACTs is “absence confirmation” or “clearing a room” i.e., to verify that a certain facility/room/warehouse does not contain a radiological source because such sourcescouldconfusemeasurements, particularlythosebeingconductedusinginformationbarriers, which are methods/CONOPs that allow non-sensitive information to be shared while the sensitive information/data is kept hidden (and then perhaps destroyed after the verification). It is tempting to assume that ACT verification should only be done using the crudest of measurement techniques which do not collect sensitive data (and are also prone to errors and subterfuge), but that need not be so. It is theoretically LBNL Report #2001653 possible to collect information-rich data (which will have sensitive information in it), extract non- sensitive information from it (e.g., counts of radiological sources) and share it with an inspector while keeping the sensitive information hidden. The existence and enforcement of information barriers is critical to the use of rich datasets in ACT verification activities. They allow the use of multimodal information necessary for accurate counting of NW devices, while keeping sensitive information secret.
